title: Decouple operator-claim-cache, introduce KMS ephemeral witness and audit-compact pipeline
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: Reduce blast radius for operator scope decisions and improve audit ingestion throughput for high-volume tenants. This PR decouples the in-memory operator-claim-cache into a small local read-optimized store plus an optional decentralized assertions layer, adds an ephemeral KMS "witness" flow for short-lived attestation tokens to reduce long-term key exposure, and implements an audit-compact pipeline that batches and cryptographically stamps compacted audit bundles before forwarding to upstream ingestion. The changes aim to improve compliance proofability while reducing KMS surface area and audit storage cost. What changed: 1) operator-claim-cache split: introduced local readonly cache with a pluggable backend adapter; added TTL-driven invalidation and a guarded refresh path to avoid thundering-herd effects; 2) kms-ephemeral-witness: new KMS orchestration component issues ephemeral attestation tokens scoped to a single request window and signs a compact claim digest; the runtime attaches the witness proof to audit bundles and to operator decision headers; 3) audit-compact pipeline: a new background service compacts per-tenant audit events into time-windowed bundles, computes a Merkle root, and signs the root with the ephemeral witness; bundles are forwarded with a minimal envelope and a compact provenance header; 4) telemetry and operator safety: added metrics for witness issuance latency, compacting throughput, cache miss hotpath counter, and new SLOs for audit-forward latency; 5) migration: graceful rollout with feature flag and canary route that falls back to full audit forwarding and long-lived KMS signing until attestation volume reaches threshold. Backwards compatibility: the attachment format is additive (new provenance header) and the full audit stream remains available for rollout; the KMS witness is optional per-tenant. Security considerations: ephemeral witness reduces lifetime of signing keys and limits key usage to a short window; the decentralized cache removes a single shared cache hotpath and reduces operator-scope blast radius. Testing: unit tests for adapter abstraction, integration tests for witness issuance against a dev KMS shim, load test scenario for compacting throughput. Rollout plan: staged canary by tenant-residency region, monitor witness error rate and audit-drop metrics before broad enablement. Related: ENG-1452, PM-322. Merge: squash and merge to main.

b2e7d11: add kms-ephemeral-witness orchestrator and signing client (dev KMS shim)
c3d4f8a: implement audit-compact service and bundle envelope + provenance header
d4a5e9b: add metrics, SLO probes, and feature flag gating for rollout

review_comments: Jordan Lee (reviewer): How does the local cache handle clock skew across nodes? Concerned that TTL jitter could cause inconsistent denies during rollouts. Suggested adding a small leader-based refresh and documented fallback policy.

Maya Singh (author): Added leader refresh jitter and clarified fallback path in the description. The cache refresh uses a randomized backoff and a 'soft-stale' window so decisions continue to use slightly stale claims until refresh completes.
Priya Desai (security): Need explicit wording on KMS key usage limits and audit retention of ephemeral tokens. Asked to ensure ephemeral keys cannot be used for non-attestation operations.

Maya Singh (author): Confirmed the orchestrator requests KMS keys with constraints (purpose=attestation, ttl=5m, usage=sign-only) and we added enforcement in the KMS shim. Also added E2E test that rejects misuse attempts.

Alex Novak (ops): Observability looks good but the compacting service may delay forwarding under backpressure. Recommend a circuit-breaker and emergency-fallthrough to raw forwarding which we added in the latest push.
Raj Patel (approver): Verified integration tests in CI, load test results look fine for the canary size. Approving with one follow-up to add a migration playbook to runbook-owner. APPROVED
release_notes: Adds a pluggable operator claim cache with decentralized adapter, an ephemeral KMS witness flow to reduce key exposure, and an audit-compact pipeline that batches and cryptographically stamps audit bundles. Rollout is gated by feature flag and tenant canary.
